shared: The Phalanx is a heavy battle armor suit developed by Irian Technologies for the Free Worlds League Military. Entering production in 3065, the design filled a gap in the FWLM’s battle armor roster for a heavier platform capable of delivering sustained ranged firepower. Weighing 1,500 kilograms, the suit trades jump capability for ground speed and mounting flexibility, allowing troopers to ride OmniMechs into combat while retaining the ability to handle infantry-scale weapons. Advanced stealth protection makes the suit considerably harder to detect and engage than most contemporary heavy designs, though this comes at the cost of reduced overall durability.

The Phalanx C configuration shifts the suit into an indirect fire support role, mounting a heavy mortar alongside a copy of the Magshot gauss rifle. The mortar allows troopers to deliver fire from behind cover and over obstacles, a capability few battle armor designs can match. The Magshot provides direct-fire backup with respectable accuracy at medium range.

This loadout transforms the suit from a frontline skirmisher into a fire support platform, though the mortar’s minimum range and relatively low rate of fire demand careful positioning. Mobility and defensive characteristics remain unchanged from the base chassis: 22 km/h ground movement, improved stealth armor for reduced sensor visibility, and the standard battle claw and armored glove combination for OmniMech transport and infantry weapon handling. The configuration lacks anti-BattleMech capability, relying instead on standoff distance and its stealth profile for survivability.

The Free Worlds League Military began development of a heavy battle armor suit in 3059, seeking a domestic counter to designs like the Kanazuchi and Gnome. Irian Technologies led the effort, but persistent technical failures stalled the program for over two years. Processor malfunctions and myomer musculature breakdowns proved particularly resistant to resolution. The FWLM eventually permitted Word of Blake technical teams to join the project, and the Blakist scientists resolved the remaining issues with striking efficiency.

Production commenced in 3065 at Irian Technologies’ facilities on Irian, with the Word of Blake receiving purchasing rights as payment for their assistance. Free Worlds Defense Industries on Gibson began manufacturing shortly afterward, producing both the original configuration and a dedicated Blakist variant. During the Jihad, the Word of Blake expanded its use of the suit as a heavy fire support complement to lighter Purifier and Nighthawk designs. Alys Rousset-Marik’s resistance movement also acquired significant numbers of the original configuration, using them to provide fire support against protectorate militias.

Post-Jihad production continued under new political oversight. A second Irian BattleMechs Unlimited facility on Washburn came online around 3078, and the design remained in active service through the Dark Age. A modernized configuration appeared around 3132, proving popular with garrison and patrol commands across multiple successor states.

The modernized Phalanx D strips the suit’s missile and gauss weaponry in favor of a single detachable medium variable speed pulse laser. This energy weapon provides flexible engagement profiles, with adjustable pulse rates allowing troopers to balance accuracy against raw damage output depending on combat conditions. The simplified armament eliminates ammunition dependency, reducing logistical demands compared to earlier configurations.

A single battle claw replaces the original’s mixed manipulator arrangement, maintaining OmniMech transport capability. The base chassis characteristics carry forward: 22 km/h ground speed, improved stealth armor, and no jump capability. The configuration sacrifices the ranged versatility of earlier variants for a self-contained energy platform that can operate for extended periods without resupply, making it well suited for garrison and patrol duties where ammunition supply lines may be unreliable.

The P-5000 PowerLoader is an industrial exoskeleton produced by Waytani, Inc., a Free Worlds League corporation formed specifically to manufacture and market the design. Introduced in 3054, the 400-kilogram humanoid suit was built for cargo handling in commercial docking facilities and industrial warehouses. The PowerLoader distinguished itself from competing loader exoskeletons by offering both operator protection and greater mobility, appealing to buyers who valued worker safety alongside raw lifting capacity. The design earned a strong commercial reputation as one of the Inner Sphere's premier cargo loading platforms.

The P-5000 trades some raw lifting capacity for improved mobility and operator safety. Its paired cargo lifter manipulators handle loads of up to two metric tons, and the suit moves at roughly double the walking speed of competing loader designs. Fifty kilograms of standard armor protect the operator from falling cargo, shifting loads, and other common workplace hazards that leave unarmored exoskeleton operators vulnerable. A cutting torch provides basic utility for opening containers and cutting through packing materials.

At 400 kilograms, the PowerLoader occupies the same weight class as its primary rival but distributes that mass differently, prioritizing the operator's speed and survivability over maximum payload. The lack of jump capability is typical for loader-class exoskeletons, where stability under load matters more than vertical mobility. The result is a loader well suited to fast-paced commercial docking facilities where both efficiency and safety standards are high.

Waytani, Inc. was established in the Free Worlds League with one purpose: producing and selling the P-5000 PowerLoader. The company found immediate success in the League and Capellan Confederation, where the design's combination of mobility and operator protection appealed to industrial buyers willing to trade some lifting capacity for a more capable platform. Waytani's aggressive holovid advertising campaign during the mid-3050s proved remarkably effective, generating enough revenue to fund construction of a second manufacturing facility on Pollux in 3060.

The PowerLoader and General Motors' HeavyHauler became the two dominant loader exoskeletons on the commercial market. Both designs featured distinctive lifter arm configurations that drew numerous imitators, though court rulings across the Inner Sphere consistently upheld the original manufacturers' intellectual property. Following the Jihad, Waytani leveraged its exoskeleton expertise to develop the Exo HaulerMech, an ultralight IndustrialMech intended for the same heavy-lifting role in more demanding environments. The PowerLoader itself remained a fixture at commercial loading facilities across the Inner Sphere.

The Purifier Adaptive is a medium battle armor design developed by the Word of Blake, built around a mimetic armor system capable of shifting color to match its surroundings. First fielded in 3062 from the Krupp Armament Works on Terra, the suit was among the first combat systems to employ adaptive camouflage technology, allowing troopers to become nearly invisible when stationary. Though lightly protected compared to other medium suits, the Purifier compensates with stealth and jump capability, filling a specialized reconnaissance and infiltration role. Its unique capabilities have made the Purifier one of the most distinctive battle armor suits in service across the Inner Sphere.

The Laser configuration equips the Purifier Adaptive's modular weapon port with an extended-range small laser, the suit's only vehicle-scale armament option. This energy weapon requires no ammunition, allowing troopers to sustain fire through extended engagements without logistical concerns. Combined with the mimetic armor, which makes stationary troopers exceptionally difficult to target, the Laser configuration excels at patient ambush tactics where concealment outweighs raw firepower. The suit's battle claw enables anti-BattleMech attacks during swarming operations, and jump jets provide ninety-meter leaps for rapid repositioning. Protection is relatively light for a medium suit, trading armor mass for the camouflage system that defines the design. The Laser loadout is considered the most self-sufficient configuration, requiring no resupply in the field.

The origins of the Purifier Adaptive trace to ComStar's Sandhurst Royal Military College on Terra, where scientists began developing mimetic color-shifting technology for infantry use in 3058. When elements of the Word of Blake overran the college, the Sandhurst Training Regiment fought to defend it but could not prevent the research data from falling into enemy hands. ComStar believed the project had been destroyed along with the facility.

Word of Blake engineers had gained considerable experience in battle armor development through their joint program with the Free Worlds League Military to produce the Achileus light suit. That expertise proved critical in adapting ComStar's mimetic research into a functional battle armor camouflage system. Development proceeded at the Krupp Armament Works in Germany, where Blakist technicians refined the technology through extensive testing before settling on a final production design. A prototype was revealed in August 3061, and the Purifier entered full production the following year.

Production at Krupp proceeded at an advanced pace, with the Word of Blake placing large quantities of the suit into every Division. The Purifier quickly earned a feared reputation during the Jihad, where its camouflage capabilities made it deadly in ambush operations and urban fighting. Troopers learned to exploit the suit's stealth by holding position until targets entered effective range, then striking before the enemy could react. Field commanders learned to manage the suit's operational limitations through disciplined tactical doctrine, maximizing the camouflage advantage under favorable conditions.

Following the liberation of Terra and the dissolution of the Word of Blake, significant numbers of Purifier suits fell into Coalition hands. The Republic of the Sphere proved the most enthusiastic adopter, capturing enough suits to equip multiple formations within the Republic Armed Forces. Republic commanders reorganized their Purifier troopers into four-member squads, mirroring standard Inner Sphere infantry doctrine rather than the Blakist six-trooper formation structure. Aside from this organizational change, the Republic operated the suit identically to the original Word of Blake configuration.

Production eventually expanded beyond Terra. HDF Manufacturing on Falsterbo began producing the Purifier Adaptive during the later Republic era, and additional manufacturers including Brevard Industries and Paragon Defense also took up production to meet growing demand. By the ilClan era, the Purifier Adaptive had spread well beyond its Blakist origins, finding service with multiple factions who valued its unique stealth capabilities.

The Narc configuration mounts a compact Narc missile beacon launcher in the Purifier Adaptive's modular weapon port, transforming the suit into a dedicated missile spotter. The launcher carries a single reload, and its bulk prevents the trooper from executing anti-BattleMech attacks or using jump jets until the ammunition is expended and the launcher jettisoned. This significant limitation restricts mobility during the approach phase of any engagement. Once a Narc beacon is attached to a target, allied missile platforms gain a substantial accuracy bonus against the marked unit. The mimetic armor helps Narc-equipped troopers close to effective range undetected, compensating somewhat for the temporary loss of jump capability. After the launcher is jettisoned, the trooper regains full mobility but is left with only the suit's battle claw for offensive action.

The PPC configuration is the newest addition to the Purifier Adaptive's weapon options, mounting an infantry-scale support particle projector cannon in the modular weapon port. Though classified as an infantry weapon rather than a vehicle-scale system, the PPC provides effective standoff capability that pairs well with the suit's mimetic armor. Troopers can remain motionless and nearly invisible at range while delivering accurate fire, making this the preferred loadout for sniping operations. The suit retains its battle claw for close-quarters anti-BattleMech attacks and jump jets for ninety-meter repositioning leaps. As with all Purifier configurations, armor protection is light for a medium suit, but the PPC's engagement range allows troopers to keep hostile units at a distance where the thin armor matters less.

The TAG configuration equips the Purifier Adaptive's modular weapon port with a light target acquisition gear system, enabling troopers to designate targets for artillery strikes and semi-guided missile fire from allied units. This configuration carries no direct-fire weapons beyond the suit's battle claw, relying entirely on supporting forces for offensive action. The mimetic armor proves especially valuable in this role, as TAG operators must maintain line of sight to their targets while remaining undetected. Jump jets provide ninety-meter leaps for reaching elevated observation positions, and the trooper's low signature allows extended spotting without drawing counterfire. The TAG loadout demands coordination with artillery and missile assets, making it less useful for independent operations but devastating when integrated into a combined-arms force.

The Quirinus is a medium-weight Inner Sphere battle armor produced by StarCorp Industries on Terra. Entering service in 3093, the suit was designed as a general-purpose trooper platform for the open market rather than exclusive military procurement. Its medium frame balances protection and mobility, offering jump-capable movement and armor well suited to its weight class. A modular weapon mount allows field commanders to tailor the suit's primary armament to mission requirements, giving the Quirinus a generalist flexibility valued by military and mercenary organizations alike.

The David Light Gauss Rifle configuration gives the Quirinus a long-range precision strike capability uncommon among medium battle armor. The rifle's ballistic reach allows troopers to engage targets at distances where most battle armor weapons fall short, while the suit's integral Light TAG designator enables effective coordination with supporting artillery and missile units. Four hundred eighty kilograms of reactive armor provide strong protection against explosive ordnance, though the suit remains more vulnerable to direct energy weapon fire. A vibro-enhanced battle claw on the right arm allows anti-BattleMech swarming attacks, and jump jets provide ninety meters of leaping mobility to offset the suit's modest ten kilometer per hour ground speed.

The Quirinus lacks an anti-personnel weapon mount, leaving troopers reliant on their primary armament and battle claw against unarmored infantry. This configuration favors engagements at range, where the David rifle and TAG coordination can soften targets before close contact becomes necessary.

StarCorp Industries developed the Quirinus at their Terra facility during the early Republic era, with the first production models entering service in 3093. Rather than restricting sales to the Republic Armed Forces, StarCorp marketed the suit broadly, finding eager buyers among the fractured provinces of the former Free Worlds League. The League's successor states, each maintaining independent military forces, welcomed a reliable medium battle armor that could fill generalist roles across varied operational environments.

Mercenary commands also proved enthusiastic customers, with some units accepting Quirinus suits as partial payment for contracts. The suit's combination of solid protection and a flexible weapon system made it attractive to organizations that needed adaptability without specialized logistics chains. By the mid-thirty-second century, the Quirinus had spread across much of the Inner Sphere's mercenary market and several provincial militaries, earning a quiet reputation as a dependable workhorse rather than a showpiece.

The Heavy Grenade Launcher configuration trades the long-range precision of the David rifle for flexible area-effect firepower at shorter distances. The launcher's ability to deliver explosive payloads across a wide engagement zone makes this configuration effective against clustered infantry, light vehicles, and entrenched positions. Paired with the suit's integral Light TAG designator, troopers can mark targets for supporting fire while simultaneously suppressing them with grenade bursts. Four hundred eighty kilograms of reactive armor absorb explosive impacts well, complementing the close-to-medium range role this configuration typically fills.

Jump jets allow ninety meters of leaping movement per burst, critical for closing distance and repositioning between volleys. The vibro battle claw provides a credible anti-BattleMech capability in swarming attacks, though the grenade launcher's limited ammunition supply demands careful fire discipline. Without an anti-personnel weapon mount, troopers must rely on the launcher's splash damage against soft targets.

The Machine Gun configuration, introduced in 3138, adds a high-volume ballistic option to the Quirinus weapon family. The machine gun excels at suppressing infantry and engaging light targets with sustained fire, making this the most effective anti-personnel loadout available for the suit. The integral Light TAG designator complements the machine gun's suppressive role by allowing troopers to guide indirect fire onto hardened targets that resist small-arms fire. Reactive armor totaling four hundred eighty kilograms shields the trooper from explosive threats, though energy weapons bypass this protection entirely.

Jump capability of ninety meters per leap offsets the slow ground pace of ten kilometers per hour, enabling troopers to reposition quickly between engagements. The vibro battle claw retains the suit's anti-BattleMech swarming potential, giving this configuration a broader target profile than either the David or grenade launcher loadouts. Ammunition consumption remains the primary constraint during extended operations.

The Raiden is a medium-weight battle armor developed by the Draconis Combine as an improvement on the Inner Sphere Standard design. Produced by Luthien Armor Works and New Samarkand Metals, the suit entered full production in 3055 after an intensive development program that began with captured Clan technology. Jump-capable and heavily armored for its weight class, the Raiden carries a modular weapon mount that accepts a range of infantry-scale weapons, along with a battle claw for anti-BattleMech operations and OmniMech transport. The suit became the preferred powered armor of the DCMS, earning a fearsome reputation across decades of service with the Dragon's infantry forces.

The anti-infantry configuration replaces the standard modular weapon mount with a fixed loadout optimized for close-quarters urban combat. Both a flamer and machine gun are mounted alongside an upgraded vibro-claw, giving the trooper devastating anti-personnel capability at short range. The vibro-claw's molecular-edge blade tears through conventional body armor and light structures with ease, making this variant particularly feared in building-to-building fighting. Jump jets retain the standard ninety-meter capability, allowing troopers to clear obstacles and gain rooftop positions during urban operations. The suit carries the same polymer-bonded armor as other production Raiden variants, providing heavy protection appropriate for the close engagements this configuration is designed to seek out. The dual-weapon approach sacrifices the flexibility of the modular mount for concentrated lethality against infantry and unarmored targets, making this a specialist configuration rather than a general-purpose loadout.

The Raiden traces its origins to the Battle of Wolcott in 3050, where overconfident Smoke Jaguar commanders lost twenty-four pristine Elemental battlesuits to Draconis Combine forces. The DCMS seized on this windfall and began reverse-engineering the captured technology almost immediately, with formal development commencing in November of that year.

The first prototype emerged in April 3052 and was presented to Coordinator Takashi Kurita in a live-fire demonstration that June. While the suit offered decent ground speed, jump capability, and respectable protection for its era, the Coordinator found it lacking. He directed the project team to redesign the suit so that a trooper could survive a direct hit from a large laser, and commanded the team's seventy-year-old director, Dr. Guthrie, to personally wear the prototype during its next trial.

Nine months of intensive work followed. The development team achieved the Coordinator's demanding armor threshold through a breakthrough in polymer bonding techniques, though the improvement required removing the suit's missile launcher. The trade-off proved worthwhile on multiple counts, as the removal also improved the suit's balance and handling characteristics. Dr. Guthrie donned the redesigned prototype for a live-fire exercise in February 3053. Lacking the physical conditioning or training to properly control the powered armor, the elderly scientist nonetheless marched onto the firing range and endured a barrage of laser and missile fire. The suit held together, barely, and Dr. Guthrie survived with five broken bones and a month-long hospital stay. The Coordinator rewarded his dedication with a promotion to head of the ISF's Research and Development department. When Dr. Guthrie passed away a year later, he was laid to rest with a full honor guard of Raiden-equipped infantrymen.

Full-scale production began in January 3055 at Luthien Armor Works, with New Samarkand Metals establishing a second production line shortly thereafter. The Raiden quickly became the common symbol of DCMS armored infantry, supplanting the Inner Sphere Standard in Combine service. Where the Standard had been a rushed effort to field any battle armor at all, the Raiden reflected the Combine's determination to produce a suit worthy of the Dragon's warriors. Its success encouraged further battle armor development within the DCMS, with the experiences and lessons learned from the Raiden program directly inspiring the lighter Kage reconnaissance suit and the heavier Kanazuchi assault armor.

The suit's modular weapon mount proved one of its most practical features, allowing field commanders to tailor loadouts to mission requirements without requiring factory modification. Additional weapon options expanded over time, with the Tsunami Heavy Gauss Rifle becoming available in 3056 and a compact medium-range missile launcher following in 3064. An urban combat variant mounting enhanced close-quarters weaponry entered service in 3058, initially as a field modification before transitioning to factory production.

Raiden-equipped infantry earned a fearsome reputation during the FedCom Civil War and the Jihad. Units such as the Dragonslayers of the Seventy-first Mechanized Infantry and the Soulsuckers of the Second Genyosha Infantry distinguished themselves repeatedly against both conventional forces and Word of Blake troops. The suit's combination of durability, mobility, and flexible armament ensured it remained a frontline asset for the DCMS well into the Dark Age, with both Luthien and New Samarkand continuing production runs across multiple decades.

The original Raiden prototype mounts a fixed small laser in the right arm alongside a shoulder-mounted single-shot SRM launcher. This early configuration predates the modular weapon mount of the production model, carrying both weapons simultaneously rather than offering field-swappable options. The SRM launcher provides a one-use punch against hardened targets, after which the trooper relies on the small laser and battle claw for continued combat. Jump jets deliver ninety meters of leap capability, matching the Clan Elemental suit that inspired the design. The prototype's armor protection, while impressive for its era, falls short of the production model's polymer-bonded standard. The SRM launcher's weight and its impact on the suit's balance were among the factors that led to its removal during the redesign process, resulting in the heavier-armored production Raiden that entered service three years later.

The flamer configuration mounts a battle armor-scale flamer in the suit's right-arm modular weapon mount. This loadout excels at clearing fortified positions and engaging conventional infantry, where the flamer's area-effect coverage compensates for its limited range. The left arm carries a battle claw that allows troopers to make anti-BattleMech attacks and ride OmniMechs into combat. Three jump jets provide ninety meters of jump capability, giving troopers the mobility to exploit vertical terrain and close rapidly with entrenched defenders. The suit's 450 kilograms of standard armor, achieved through an advanced polymer bonding process, can absorb a direct hit from a large pulse laser while keeping the trooper combat-effective. At one thousand kilograms total mass, the Raiden sits at the upper limit for mechanized battle armor operations, trading the lighter profile of scout suits for substantially greater protection and striking power.

The laser configuration equips the Raiden's right-arm modular weapon mount with a small laser. This energy weapon provides reliable firepower without ammunition dependency, making it well-suited for extended operations and garrison duty where resupply may be limited. The small laser's accuracy at close range also makes it effective against other battle armor and light vehicles. As with all standard Raiden configurations, the suit retains its left-arm battle claw for anti-BattleMech attacks and OmniMech transport, three jump jets providing ninety meters of leap capability, and 450 kilograms of polymer-bonded armor protection. The laser variant's freedom from ammunition concerns comes at the cost of reduced anti-infantry effectiveness compared to area-effect weapons, making it less ideal for clearing entrenched conventional forces but more dependable across prolonged engagements.

The machine gun configuration fits a battle armor-scale machine gun into the Raiden's right-arm modular weapon mount. The weapon delivers sustained ballistic fire effective against conventional infantry and soft targets, with ammunition capacity sufficient for extended engagements. Against hardened targets the machine gun offers less penetration than energy weapons, but its high rate of fire and suppressive capability make it a preferred choice for infantry support operations. The suit's standard combat systems remain unchanged from other Raiden configurations: a left-arm battle claw for anti-BattleMech attacks and OmniMech transport, three jump jets delivering ninety meters of jump capability, and 450 kilograms of polymer-bonded standard armor. The machine gun's reliance on ammunition introduces a logistical dependency absent in energy weapon loadouts, though DCMS quartermasters generally considered the trade-off acceptable given the weapon's raw effectiveness against unarmored targets.

The medium-range missile configuration mounts a compact single-tube MRM launcher with four reloads in the Raiden's right-arm modular weapon mount. Developed during the FedCom Civil War era and entering service in 3064, this loadout provides indirect fire capability rare among medium battle armor. The missile launcher's range advantage allows Raiden troopers to engage targets at distances where most battle armor weapons fall short, though the single-tube design limits its volume of fire per salvo. The suit otherwise retains its full combat suite, including jump jets for ninety-meter leaps, a left-arm battle claw enabling anti-BattleMech attacks and mechanized transport, and heavy polymer-bonded armor rated to withstand large energy weapon impacts. Ammunition dependency and the weapon's modest per-shot damage output represent the primary limitations of this configuration.

The Tsunami configuration arms the Raiden with a Tsunami Heavy Gauss Rifle in its right-arm modular weapon mount. Available from 3056, this ballistic weapon delivers exceptional stopping power for a battle armor platform, capable of threatening light vehicles and other armored infantry at respectable ranges. The heavy gauss rifle's kinetic impact makes it one of the more powerful options available to Raiden troopers, though its ammunition supply is finite and the weapon adds considerable weight to the already heavy suit. Standard Raiden combat systems complement the Tsunami's firepower: jump jets provide ninety meters of mobility, a battle claw on the left arm supports anti-BattleMech operations and OmniMech mounting, and the suit's advanced polymer-bonded armor absorbs significant punishment before failing. The Tsunami variant fills a fire support role, engaging harder targets that lighter weapon loadouts struggle to damage.

The Raiden II is a Dark Age-era upgrade of the Draconis Combine's long-serving Raiden battle armor. Produced by New Samarkand Metals, the suit features upgraded armor protection and an additional weapon mount, addressing limitations identified through decades of operational experience with the original design. The upgrade retains the Raiden's proven jump capability and battle claw, maintaining compatibility with established DCMS infantry doctrine. Introduced around 3123, the Raiden II gave Combine armored infantry improved survivability without requiring a complete redesign of the familiar Raiden platform.

The Raiden II's flamer configuration carries a battle armor-scale flamer as its primary weapon, paired with the anti-personnel weapon mount that distinguishes the Raiden II from its predecessor. The suit's most significant upgrade is its reflective armor, which disperses energy weapon impacts more effectively than the original Raiden's polymer-bonded standard plating. Against laser-heavy opponents this protection gives Raiden II troopers a meaningful survivability advantage, though the reflective coating offers reduced protection against ballistic and explosive weapons compared to conventional armor of equivalent weight. Jump jets maintain the ninety-meter leap capability inherited from the original Raiden, and the left-arm battle claw retains full anti-BattleMech attack and OmniMech transport functionality. The flamer's area-effect fire combined with the anti-personnel mount makes this configuration effective for clearing infantry positions, particularly in environments where energy weapons are the primary threat.

The Raiden II emerged from the Draconis Combine's growing embrace of reflective armor technology during the early thirty-second century. The Kishi battle armor had demonstrated the value of reflective plating against energy-heavy opponents, and DCMS procurement officers quickly authorized a similar upgrade for the long-serving Raiden chassis. New Samarkand Metals received the contract, producing an updated suit that replaced the standard polymer-bonded armor with reflective plating while adding an anti-personnel weapon mount absent from the original design. The Raiden II entered production around 3123 and saw deployment with frontline DCMS formations during the turbulent Dark Age period. While not a radical redesign, the upgrade ensured that Combine battle armor infantry retained an edge against energy-weapon-equipped opponents, extending the Raiden platform's service life well beyond what its original designers likely envisioned.

The heavy machine gun configuration arms the Raiden II with a weapon offering greater penetration and stopping power than the standard machine gun available to the original Raiden. The heavy machine gun's increased caliber makes it effective against lightly armored vehicles and battle armor in addition to conventional infantry, broadening the suit's engagement envelope. Like the flamer variant, this configuration benefits from the Raiden II's reflective armor, which provides enhanced resistance to energy weapons at the cost of reduced protection against ballistic impacts. The anti-personnel weapon mount adds a secondary close-range option absent from original Raiden designs. Standard mobility systems carry over from the base Raiden platform, with jump jets providing ninety meters of leap capability and a battle claw enabling anti-BattleMech attacks and mechanized transport. The heavy machine gun's ammunition demands require careful supply management, but its hitting power makes the trade-off attractive for Combine infantry commanders.

The Ravager is an assault-class battle armor produced by Marian Arms Incorporated on Horatius in the Marian Hegemony. Introduced in 3084, the suit was designed using common Inner Sphere technology to fill both a domestic defense role and generate export revenue for the small Periphery nation. The Ravager gained rapid popularity among mercenary commands and smaller states, earning a reputation as a rugged and affordable heavy combat suit. While widely acknowledged as one of the least attractive battle armor designs in production, the combination of heavy protection and an accessible price point has ensured steady demand across the Inner Sphere and beyond.

The Ravager traces its origins to the brief alliance between the Marian Hegemony and the Word of Blake. During the Jihad, the Blakists had begun upgrading the Marian Arms facility on Horatius, including construction of a battle armor production line. When Caesar Julius O'Reilly evicted the Word from his nation, the partially completed facility sat dormant for years. After the Jihad, Doctor Dafyyd Rou, a former employee of Irian Technologies, fled into Marian space. Caesar Cassius O'Reilly tasked Rou with completing the facility and producing a new suit for both Hegemony defense and export sales. The development program nearly bankrupted the small Periphery nation, but Rou delivered a functional assault suit by 3084.

Within a year the Ravager had become the most sought-after battle armor on the open markets. The Marian government sold the suit to any willing buyer, channeling profits back into the Horatius factory and further research. Mercenary commands and smaller states proved eager customers, with independent nations in the former Free Worlds League showing particular interest. An upgraded variant with indirect fire capability entered production around 3101, sustaining export demand well into the Dark Age.
