The Ravager is a two-ton assault suit built with common Inner Sphere technology and modified BattleMech armor plating. Its primary weapon is a multi-barrel heavy recoilless rifle mounted on the right arm, featuring redundant barrels that allow continued operation even after sustaining damage. Two single-tube rocket launchers on the main body provide supplemental firepower, while a battle claw on the left arm handles close-quarters work. Protection is the suit's defining characteristic, with nearly a full metric ton of standard armor giving operators confidence against all but the heaviest autocannon fire. Ground speed reaches a respectable twenty kilometers per hour, quick for a suit of this weight class.

The Ravager lacks jump capability entirely, limiting its tactical mobility in rough terrain. Many observers consider the overall firepower modest for an assault-class design, and the suit has earned a reputation as one of the least visually appealing battle armor in service. Operators have taken to calling it "the Waddle," though most are willing to trade aesthetics for the survivability it offers.

The Resgate is a Clan-manufactured light exoskeleton designed exclusively for search and rescue operations. Developed by Clan Cloud Cobra's scientist caste in the early thirtieth century, the suit was built to improve emergency response capabilities across Cobra-held worlds. Carrying no weapons, the Resgate prioritized sensor capability, debris-clearing tools, and operator protection over any form of combat effectiveness. The design earned a strong reputation among emergency services personnel for its reliability under harsh and dangerous field conditions.

The Interdictor configuration replaces the Resgate's sensor suite and salvage arm with an electronic countermeasures package and a pair of armored gloves. Developed during the Jihad, this variant shifts the exoskeleton's role from rescue operations to electronic warfare support. The ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting systems and communications within its effective radius, providing valuable cover for friendly forces operating nearby.

Armored gloves replace the specialized manipulators of the base model, sacrificing debris-clearing capability for improved manual dexterity in field conditions. The suit retains its fire-resistant armor and jump jets, maintaining the mobility and thermal protection of the original design. Without sensors or salvage equipment, the Interdictor cannot perform rescue operations. It fills a niche role as a lightweight, mobile ECM platform that can accompany infantry formations into terrain too restrictive for larger electronic warfare vehicles.

In the late thirtieth century, a massive earthquake struck the Cloud Cobra enclave on Homer, killing over eight hundred merchant and laborer caste members and devastating a quarter of the settlement. The Warrior Council, shaken by the scale of the disaster, directed the scientist caste to develop improved emergency response tools. Working from castoff battle armor prototypes, Cloud Cobra scientists produced a compact light exoskeleton stripped down to the essentials needed for locating and extracting trapped or injured civilians.

The suit's protective capabilities expanded following a trial between Cloud Cobra and Clan Fire Mandrill scientists. Scientist Carl of the Cloud Cobras won access to fire-resistant armor technology through a magnetic belt experiment, and the material was quickly integrated into the Resgate design. The 849th Fire Response Unit validated the upgrade when the DropShip Dresden crashed on Babylon. Resgate operators pulled nearly the entire crew from the burning wreckage, losing only a single life.

During the Jihad, Cloud Cobra engineers developed four specialized variants that expanded the exoskeleton's role beyond rescue operations into electronic warfare, reconnaissance, target designation, and fire support. Production later spread to Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten under Clan Jade Falcon control.

The Scout configuration retains the improved sensor suite of the base Resgate while replacing the salvage arm with armored gloves. This variant preserves the exoskeleton's reconnaissance capability while providing better manual dexterity for field operations. The sensor suite maintains its ability to detect life signs and gather environmental data, making the Scout useful for both forward reconnaissance and search operations.

Armored gloves give the operator improved grip and handling compared to the salvage arm, allowing for more versatile fieldwork. The suit keeps its fire-resistant armor and jump jets, offering the same thermal protection and mobility as the standard model. Without the salvage arm, the Scout cannot efficiently clear heavy debris, limiting its effectiveness in pure rescue scenarios. The configuration works best as a forward observer or pathfinder, scouting ahead of rescue teams to locate survivors and assess conditions before committing heavier equipment.

The Spotter configuration strips the Resgate's standard equipment in favor of a light TAG designator and armored gloves. This Jihad-era variant transforms the rescue exoskeleton into a forward targeting platform, capable of painting targets for artillery and missile strikes. The light TAG unit allows the operator to designate targets for semi-guided munitions from positions that heavier spotting platforms cannot reach.

Armored gloves provide adequate manual dexterity for field operations. The suit retains its fire-resistant armor and jump capability, giving it the thermal protection and mobility to operate in forward positions. Without sensors, the Spotter relies entirely on the operator's own situational awareness to locate and designate targets. The configuration sacrifices all rescue functionality for a single combat-support role, making it the most specialized of the Resgate variants.

The Resgate weighs four hundred kilograms and carries no weapons of any kind, reflecting its single-minded focus on emergency rescue. Its primary tool is an improved sensor suite capable of detecting life signs through up to ten meters of dense material, paired with a salvage arm on the left limb for clearing debris and extracting trapped personnel. A basic manipulator on the right arm handles more delicate tasks. Jump jets provide the mobility needed to reach disaster sites that ground vehicles cannot access, giving the suit a ninety-meter jump range at a ground speed of thirty kilometers per hour.

Fire-resistant armor protects the operator from intense heat for limited periods, a critical advantage during structural fires and vehicle crashes. The suit lacks any form of offensive or defensive weaponry, and its light construction offers minimal ballistic protection. Operators working in active combat zones require escort from armed units.

The Support configuration replaces all standard rescue equipment with a light machine gun and armored gloves, converting the Resgate into a light combat platform. This Jihad-era variant is the only configuration in the family that carries offensive weaponry. The light machine gun provides effective anti-infantry firepower, giving the Support variant the ability to engage unarmored targets and provide suppressive fire for friendly formations.

Armored gloves offer adequate handling for field operations and close-quarters situations. Fire-resistant armor and jump jets carry over from the base design, maintaining thermal protection and tactical mobility. The Support variant's combat capability remains modest by battle armor standards. Its light machine gun handles conventional infantry and soft targets effectively but struggles against armored opponents. The configuration fills a security role, providing armed escort for rescue teams operating in contested areas where unarmed exoskeletons would be vulnerable.

The Rogue Bear is a Clan Ghost Bear heavy battlesuit produced at BA Facility Gamma on Mannedorf. First fielded in 3073 during the closing years of the Jihad, the design fills a rapid-response role within garrison and second-line formations, offering jump capability and fixed armament suited to patrol and security operations. Weighing 1,500 kilograms, the Rogue Bear earned a reputation for reliability and low maintenance requirements, qualities that proved valuable during a period of significant logistical strain across the Ghost Bear Dominion. Several derivative designs have since been developed from the Rogue Bear chassis.

The Hybrid is a stealth-focused variant refined from the experimental HR prototype. Engineers replaced the HR's partial wing system with a jump booster providing equivalent ninety-meter range but greater reliability. Battle claws gave way to basic manipulators, freeing enough weight to double the suit's secondary armament to two machine guns and two anti-personnel weapon mounts. The Hybrid retains basic stealth armor and a camouflage system, granting reduced detection signatures at the cost of lighter protection compared to the standard Rogue Bear.

This creates a suit caught between roles: its weapons encourage close-range engagement while its stealth systems reward standoff distance. The blending of Inner Sphere and Clan technologies introduces maintenance complexity despite the suit's Easy to Maintain design, as non-standard parts can be difficult to source. Formations already operating Kobold suits have adopted the Hybrid most readily, benefiting from parts commonality with the Rogue Bear chassis.

The Rogue Bear emerged from BA Facility Gamma on Mannedorf during one of the Ghost Bear Dominion's most turbulent periods. First observed in garrison forces during December 3073, the heavy battlesuit drew immediate comparisons to the Golem. Careful analysis confirmed it as an entirely new design, built along similar lines but lighter and with a different operational emphasis. The suit entered service with KungsArmé formations absorbed into the Ghost Bear touman, with the recently activated First Tyr Assault Cluster among its earliest recipients. The First Tyr, stationed on the former Free Rasalhague Republic capital of Orestes, was primarily composed of ethnic Rasalhagians retrained in Clan organization and tactics.

Following a brutal engagement against Word of Blake forces on Radstadt in 3074, Ghost Bear commanders rewarded the First Tyr's abtakha troopers with early production Rogue Bear suits. BA Facility Gamma continued production through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, with the Rasalhague Dominion fielding the design across multiple Galaxies. The 283rd Battle Cluster, also stationed on Mannedorf, maintained strong contingents and employed them effectively against Draconis Combine border raids. The chassis proved adaptable, spawning the Constable Pacification Suit and the Wraith battle armor, which was originally prototyped as a Rogue Bear variant.

The Rogue Bear is a heavy battlesuit weighing 1,500 kilograms, built around a fixed weapons loadout with no disposable components. Its primary anti-vehicle armament is a three-tube short-range missile launcher hardwired to its back, carrying four reloads. Two arm-mounted machine guns provide effective anti-infantry firepower. For close combat and OmniMech transport capability, the suit employs vibro-blade-enhanced battle claw manipulators. Jump jets allow sixty-meter leaps under terrestrial gravity.

The suit carries enough standard armor to nearly absorb a Gauss rifle hit, though this protection comes at the cost of reduced sophistication compared to heavier assault designs. The emphasis on standard, non-disposable components reflects a practical design philosophy, reducing logistical strain on garrison formations operating far from primary supply lines. The fixed missile launcher does add bulk even when ammunition is expended, limiting the suit's utility in prolonged engagements where weight becomes a factor.

The Upgrade configuration trades raw firepower for improved survivability. Engineers reduced the missile launcher to a two-tube system while retaining its four-shot ammunition supply, and replaced the original vibro-blade manipulators with heavy battle claws. The freed weight and volume allowed installation of reactive armor plating across the suit's frame, providing significantly better protection against missile and ballistic threats than the standard armor of the original design.

The heavy battle claws retain OmniMech transport capability while offering strong melee performance, though they lack the cutting precision of vibro-blades. The twin machine guns carry over unchanged, maintaining the suit's anti-infantry effectiveness. This configuration shifts the Rogue Bear toward a more defensive role, better suited to holding positions and absorbing fire during close-quarters engagements where the reactive armor's properties are most effective.

The HR is an experimental prototype blending Inner Sphere and Clan technologies into a heavy reconnaissance platform. A partial wing system grants ninety-meter jump capability, while a Spheroid-designed camouflage system and basic stealth armor reduce the suit's detection profile. Offensive armament is deliberately light, limited to a single machine gun and one anti-personnel weapon mount, reflecting the HR's intended role as a scout and insurgent hunter rather than a frontline combatant. Battle claws provide OmniMech transport capability and melee options.

The fusion of Clan structural engineering with Inner Sphere stealth and sensor technologies produced mixed results during field testing. The suit's firepower was judged insufficient for its weight class, and the partial wing system proved problematic in low-atmosphere environments, limiting the HR's operational utility despite its strong reconnaissance performance.

The Rottweiler is a medium quad battle armor suit developed by TharHes Industries for the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces. Fielded in 3065, the design built on lessons learned from the earlier Fenrir program, prioritizing speed and sensor capability over raw firepower. Its low profile and advanced electronics package earned it a respected place among Lyran reconnaissance formations, where its ability to operate well ahead of heavier units proved consistently valuable across multiple theaters of operation.

The Close Combat configuration replaces the standard weapon loadout with a flamer and a machine gun while retaining the full sensor suite and mission equipment package. This combination transforms the Rottweiler into a close-quarters infantry killer, particularly effective in the tight confines of urban terrain where its 54 kph speed allows rapid repositioning through streets and alleyways.

The flamer provides area denial and building-clearing capability, while the machine gun delivers sustained anti-personnel fire. Against armored opponents the configuration remains limited, relying on speed and stealth to avoid engagements it cannot win. The retention of the integrated sensor package distinguishes this variant from a simple brawler, allowing Close Combat squads to still feed targeting data to friendly forces between engagements.

The Rottweiler grew out of a Lyran Alliance effort to push quad battle armor beyond what the Fenrir had demonstrated. TharHes Industries on Eutin led the program, directing their engineers to build a suit that could outrun any competing design while hugging the ground closely enough to frustrate enemy targeting solutions. The result entered service in 3065 as the fastest quad battlesuit in production.

Lyran commanders had initially greeted quad battle armor with skepticism, but the Rottweiler gradually won converts among LAAF reconnaissance formations during border operations against the Free Worlds League. Mixed groups of Rottweilers and Fenrir armor screened ahead of main assault forces, marking targets and feeding positional data to artillery commanders.

The Jihad forced TharHes to develop three new configurations between 3069 and 3072. One filled an urban warfare gap left by the destruction of Gray Death Battle Armor production on Glengarry. A defensive variant with remote sensors and a longer-ranged weapon proved critical during the liberation of Donegal in 3071, where mixed squads detected and ambushed a Blakist probing force. Rottweilers remained a staple of Lyran reconnaissance doctrine into the ilClan era.

The Firedrake configuration carries four Firedrake incendiary needlers and heavier armor plating than the standard model. This loadout makes the suit devastatingly effective against conventional infantry formations, capable of shredding unarmored platoons in seconds. The additional armor allows Firedrake-equipped troopers to close with infantry positions that would threaten lighter configurations.

The concentrated needler armament poses a credible threat even to BattleMechs through sheer volume of fire against exposed joints and sensors, though this remains a secondary capability. Against other battle armor or vehicles the configuration is poorly suited, as needler weapons lack the penetration to defeat proper armor plating. The Firedrake excels in its intended role of infantry suppression and area clearance.

The Rottweiler's quad chassis propels the one-ton suit to speeds of 54 kph, making it one of the fastest battle armor designs in service. Rather than the turret mount used by the Fenrir, the engineering team opted for a fixed dorsal weapon position carrying a standard support laser and a Firedrake incendiary needler for anti-personnel work. This arrangement allows the pilot to lie flat inside the chassis, reducing fatigue on extended scouting missions.

Standard stealth armor defeats most targeting systems while providing protection comparable to heavier suits despite the Rottweiler's lighter mass. An advanced sensor suite gives the suit exceptional situational awareness, and a frontal hatch mimicking the design's canine namesake can carry up to five kilograms of mission equipment. The trade-off for this sensor and speed package is limited offensive punch against armored targets.

The Upgrade configuration trades the Rottweiler's integrated sensor suite for a remote sensor dispenser, sacrificing real-time situational awareness in favor of broader area coverage. A King David light gauss rifle replaces both standard weapons, giving the suit meaningful standoff range for the first time. Mission equipment is retained.

Remote sensors scattered across a defensive perimeter allow Upgrade-equipped units to monitor a wider area than any single sensor suite could cover, feeding movement data back to command elements. The gauss rifle provides enough reach to engage targets detected by the sensor network before they close to effective range. The configuration sacrifices the stealth armor's full benefit in close engagements, as the pilot must break cover to fire, but its defensive screening capability proved highly effective in static and semi-static operations.

The Salamander is a Clan medium battle armor suit developed by Kindraa Faraday-Tanaga of Clan Fire Mandrill. Entering production in 3058, the design revived and modernized an earlier specialist suit that had been phased out in favor of the Elemental. The Salamander's emphasis on fire-based weaponry honors its creators' totem animal and gives the suit a fearsome reputation in close-quarters combat. Jump-capable and equipped with specialized climbing claws, the Salamander excels at anti-BattleMech swarming attacks despite carrying relatively light armor for its weight class. The suit has been widely adopted across Clan militaries, with several Clans producing their own tailored configurations.

The anti-infantry configuration replaces both flamers with heavy machine guns, shifting the suit's role toward raw anti-personnel lethality at the cost of its thermal threat profile. The heavy machine guns deliver punishing sustained fire against unarmored and lightly armored targets, cutting through conventional infantry formations with brutal efficiency. Against BattleMechs, the configuration loses the heat-spiking capability that makes the standard Salamander feared, though the shoulder-mounted Inferno SRM launcher still provides a single thermal punch during swarming attacks. Battle claws, magnetic foot claws, jump jets, and fire-resistant armor carry over unchanged. This configuration trades psychological intimidation for volume of fire, making it the preferred choice for garrison duty and counter-insurgency operations.

The Salamander traces its lineage to a pre-Elemental specialist design intended for urban warfare against conventional infantry. That original suit fell from favor as battlesuits supplanted the troops they were meant to fight, and few Clan warriors mourned its retirement given the perceived dishonor of anti-infantry duty. The design languished until scientists of Clan Fire Mandrill's Kindraa Faraday-Tanaga drew inspiration from Clan Hell's Horses' Gnome program. Seeking a second-generation battlesuit honoring their Clan's fiery totem, the Kindraa selected the dormant Salamander as their foundation. Chronic infighting within Faraday-Tanaga and persistent engineering challenges delayed development, but the modernized suit cleared field testing and entered production in 3058.

Battlefield effectiveness quickly overcame any lingering stigma. Within a decade, nearly every Clan had incorporated the Salamander into their toumans. Clan Wolf developed a variant favoring directed energy weapons that spread to Clans Goliath Scorpion and Snow Raven, while Clan Jade Falcon produced a configuration optimized for anti-personnel work in the late 3060s. Production expanded from the Fire Mandrill homeworld of Shadow to Clan Wolf facilities on Tranquil and Clan Jade Falcon's Olivetti Weaponry plant on Sudeten.

The laser configuration replaces the left arm's flamer with an ER Micro Laser, retaining the right arm's flamer and the shoulder-mounted Inferno SRM launcher. This trade gives the suit a more precise ranged engagement option while maintaining significant incendiary capability. The ER Micro Laser provides effective firepower at greater range than the flamer it replaces, making the configuration better suited for open terrain where closing distance exposes troopers to sustained fire. All other systems remain unchanged from the standard loadout: battle claws, magnetic foot claws for swarming attacks, jump jets with ninety-meter leap capability, and fire-resistant armor. The reduced reliance on proximity-dependent weapons gives this variant slightly greater endurance in prolonged engagements.

The Salamander is a one-ton medium battlesuit built around fire-based weaponry. A pair of 'Mech-scale flamers, one mounted beneath each arm, form the primary armament. These weapons generate enough thermal output to threaten the heat management systems of light and lighter medium BattleMechs, while proving devastating against infantry and vehicles. A single one-shot Inferno SRM launcher on the shoulder provides an additional heat spike during anti-'Mech engagements. Each arm terminates in a battle claw, and magnetic claws on the feet allow the suit to scale a BattleMech's hull as easily as walking on flat ground, making it one of the most effective swarming platforms in Clan service. Jump jets provide ninety meters of leap capability. The trade-off for this offensive package is thin armor protection, roughly half that of the Gnome. Fire-resistant plating shrugs off heat-based attacks, but the suit remains exposed to ballistic and missile fire.

The Demon series of battle armor emerged from Gibson Federated BattleMechs during the Jihad as the companion line to the Word of Blake's Celestial OmniMechs. Conceived by Precentor Vapula, the Manei Domini's engineering chief, the six Demon designs draw their names from the malevolent figures of various world mythologies. Each suit was crafted to fill a specific combat role while projecting an element of psychological terror against the Word's enemies. Fielded almost exclusively by the cybernetically enhanced Manei Domini elite, the Demons share the same unsettling visual aesthetic as their larger Celestial counterparts and were rarely encountered outside the Shadow Divisions.

The capture team variant appeared in mid-3073 as a specialized tool for seizing enemy vehicle crews and MechWarriors alive. Its defining feature is a battle armor taser mounted in a detachable weapon pack, capable of disrupting and disabling vehicles and BattleMechs through electromagnetic discharge. The heavy taser's bulk reduces the suit's ground speed to roughly 10 kilometers per hour until the pack is jettisoned. A pair of light machine guns, one in each arm, provide conventional firepower, and battle claws on both arms enable boarding actions. A searchlight carries over from the standard configuration. The stealth armor allows the capture team to approach targets undetected before delivering the disabling shock. A successful taser strike can net the Manei Domini a prisoner and salvageable equipment, making this variant as much an intelligence-gathering tool as a combat platform.

The Se'irim entered service alongside the Asura in 3072 as its stealthy complement. Named for the satyr-like beings of Hebrew folklore, the Se'irim was the second of the two medium-weight battlesuits in the Demon series, but where the Asura was built mainly to be an up-front fighter, the Se'irim was styled for stealth. It eschewed jump jets entirely in favor of fast overland mobility and sensor-defeating armor designed to deter enemy ranged attacks. The tactical logic was clear: in the combined-arms formations Vapula envisioned, the Asura and the Celestials would draw the enemy's attention while the Se'irim positioned for devastating ambushes from concealment.

This doctrine of concurrent deployment was central to the Demon program. The Djinn and Asura had both entered service with a standard combat configuration and a stealth-capable anti-infantry version specifically intended to keep opponents guessing about which variant they faced. The Se'irim extended this principle to the formation level: any Blakist task force deploying Asura troopers might also have Se'irim teams lying in wait. Combined with the flexibility of the Celestial OmniMechs and the cybernetic enhancements of the Manei Domini operators, this layered approach created a range of capabilities that proved particularly difficult for conventional forces to counter.

The Se'irim saw action across several Jihad-era theaters. On Benjamin, a junior officer in the Forty-fifth Shadow Division developed what she called the "Choir" formation, roughly analogous to a Clan Nova: two Level IIs of battle armor organized with a BattleMech as a single combined-arms unit. During the Word's 3072 conquest of Benjamin, these Choirs deployed battle armor in advance of DCMS formations, then withdrew BattleMechs far enough to place the enemy in a killing zone between them. The tactic destroyed a company of Draconis Combine BattleMechs, vehicles, and captured several dozen warriors before Clan Nova Cat forces eliminated the formation's creator during a hot combat drop later that year.

On Arc-Royal, a specialized unit designated the "Demon Hounds," attached to the Forty-third Shadow Division, included at least one Level I of Se'irim during the Forty-third's ill-fated 3072 attack. Thought destroyed during the assault, the Hounds actually went to ground on Arc-Royal and spent the next two years conducting reconnaissance and espionage strikes aimed at weakening the planetary defenses from within. Their most daring operation destroyed a Kell Hounds munitions storage compound outside Old Connaught and caused significant damage to the Arc-Royal MechWorks facilities in New Hannover.

Initial speculation held that the Word's Celestial and Demon series were intended to eventually replace current equipment across all Blakist line forces. This never materialized. The Demon suits appeared in significant numbers only among the hyper-elite Manei Domini. Whether this was because the Demons were specially made to interface with Domini cybernetics at levels most modern battle armor could not match, or whether it reflected a deeper political rift between the Domini and the regular forces, remained uncertain.

The standard Se'irim carries a light recoilless rifle in the right arm and a one-shot SRM-5 launcher, combining precise ballistic fire with a devastating missile volley. A full squad's simultaneous first strike can deliver enough ordnance to destroy a light BattleMech outright. A vibro-claw in the left arm allows troopers to follow up with lethal melee attacks against stunned or damaged targets, while a searchlight provides illumination for low-light operations. The suit eschews jump jets entirely in favor of an enhanced ground speed of 32 kilometers per hour, three times faster than most comparable battle armor on foot. Its 330 kilograms of stealth armor can stop a medium pulse laser while interfering with enemy targeting sensors. The lack of jump capability limits the Se'irim's tactical flexibility, but its combination of speed, stealth, and concentrated firepower makes it a devastating ambush platform.

The capture team Shedu carries a pair of battle armor tasers in a detachable weapon pack, giving each suit the potential to force two BattleMechs to shut down through electromagnetic overload. The risk of debilitating feedback from the tasers is considerable, though a fully crewed squad can attempt to disable up to ten enemy units in rapid succession. A Magshot Gauss rifle in the turret mount provides precision ballistic fire for sustained combat after the tasers are expended or jettisoned. The 600 kilograms of advanced armor and quad chassis are retained. The detachable pack's weight penalty slows the suit until dropped. This is one of the most aggressive capture configurations in the Demon series, trading stealth and subtlety for the raw ability to shut down multiple enemy machines and seize them intact.

The Shedu was the most radical departure from the rest of the Demon battle armor series. Named for the bull-human hybrid demons of ancient mythology, the Shedu was the only four-legged design in the entire line. Its animalistic appearance and "folded wing" armor plates conjured the same otherworldly imagery that Vapula had established across the rest of his designs, but the quadrupedal chassis represented a fundamentally different engineering approach from any of its siblings.

The Shedu was conceived as the Nephilim's faster companion. Vapula needed an assault-class suit that could keep pace with advancing Celestial OmniMech formations, and the quad chassis delivered excellent ground speed for its weight class. Other designers had taken a similar approach with quad battle armor like the Lyran Fenrir and Rottweiler, but those designs had sacrificed protection to emphasize speed and weapon payload. Vapula refused to make that trade. He ensured the Shedu carried enough armor to withstand hits from some of the heaviest weapons in common battlefield use before allocating mass to the motive systems. This left the Shedu with less space for weapons than the Fenrir, but the deficit was offset by the same tactical doctrine that drove the Demons in the same manner as their Celestial counterparts: these battlesuits were designed to operate in groups. A Shedu did not need to carry enough firepower to win alone. It needed to carry enough to fulfill its role within a combined-arms formation where Celestial OmniMechs, Demon battlesuits, and conventional forces each contributed their own piece to the whole.

The Shedu was one of the last Demons to enter service, and it remained a fairly rare sight even compared to its fellow Demon designs. It was more widely deployed among the Word of Blake's elite Shadow Divisions than the Nephilim, which suggests Vapula prioritized getting the faster assault suit into more hands to support the formations already built around Celestial OmniMechs. Like the other Demons, however, the Shedu remained firmly in the hands of the Manei Domini and never appeared in the colors of even the most prestigious and trustworthy regular Militia commands.
The TRO: 3075 entry lists a 3-slot configurable turret with a weight of 40 kg. The correct weight of 80 kg would exceed the maximum 2000 kg.

The recon Shedu is perhaps the most unusual of the type's configurations, replacing direct firepower with electronic warfare and indirect fire capability. An electronic camouflage system and light ECM suite render the suit nearly invisible to sensors, while improved sensors allow the trooper to detect enemy forces at extended range. A light mortar provides indirect fire support, enabling the squad to engage enemies from concealment without revealing their position. The 600 kilograms of advanced armor and quad chassis mobility are retained. This configuration turns the Shedu into a battlefield predator that hunts through stealth and patience rather than brute force, locating enemy formations and either eliminating soft targets with mortar fire or calling in heavier assets to deal with armored opposition.

The standard Shedu mounts a heavy recoilless rifle in a modular turret for anti-armor work, supplemented by twin heavy machine guns protruding from the suit's "head" that can shred infantry and threaten lightly armored targets at close range. The quadrupedal chassis provides stable firing platforms for the turret-mounted weapon and excellent ground speed for an assault-class design. The suit's 600 kilograms of advanced armor can withstand a Gauss rifle slug, giving it exceptional survivability for its weight class. The quad design prevents the Shedu from jumping or riding OmniMechs, and the cramped cockpit layout is more akin to a small combat vehicle than a conventional battlesuit. The combination of turret-based firepower, heavy armor, and ground mobility makes the standard Shedu effective in a variety of direct combat roles.

The Shen Long is a heavy battle armor suit produced by Hellespont Industrials for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces and the Magistracy of Canopus. Introduced in 3092, the design employs a quad chassis that provides exceptional ground speed for its weight class, paired with advanced camouflage systems that allow troopers to approach targets undetected. A reconfigurable weapon platform enables rapid loadout changes between missions, giving field commanders flexibility to tailor formations for specific tactical situations. The suit earned its name, meaning "Divine Dragon" in Chinese, for the aggressive ambush doctrine that defines its primary employment.

Built on a quad chassis weighing 1,500 kilograms, the Shen Long achieves a ground speed of 43 kilometers per hour, placing it among the fastest heavy battlesuits fielded by Inner Sphere forces. Its mimetic armor coating, at 550 kilograms, provides both physical protection and active camouflage that bends light and sensor returns around the suit's profile. The modular turret mount accepts up to 400 kilograms of weapons or equipment.

The Interdictor configuration trades direct firepower for electronic warfare capability, mounting two flamers alongside a full ECM suite. The flamers serve as effective short-range deterrents against infantry and light vehicles, while the ECM package disrupts enemy targeting systems and communications within a significant radius. This makes the Interdictor invaluable during ambush operations, where it can mask allied forces from sensor detection. The configuration's limited offensive reach and reliance on close-range weapons restrict its effectiveness in open terrain.

Hellespont Industrials developed the Shen Long on Sian, introducing the suit in 3092 to fulfill a Capellan Confederation Armed Forces requirement for a heavy battle armor platform built around ambush and interdiction tactics. Hellespont drew on existing expertise in advanced armor and modular weapon systems to deliver a quad-chassis suit that sacrificed manipulators for raw speed and a turret-mounted weapon platform. The name, meaning "Divine Dragon" in Chinese, reflected the aggressive doctrine the design was intended to enable.

The suit first proved itself during the Victoria War, when Menke Home Guard units paired Shen Long squads with Fa Shih minelaying teams to ambush a Davion BattleMech lance. The combined force lured the overconfident MechWarriors into a prepared minefield, then used multiple configurations to overwhelm and deceive the disoriented enemy, capturing an assault BattleMech in the process. On Yuris in 3103, Shen Long troopers harassed a Davion task force during weeks of fighting, though ammunition shortages forced several teams to surrender when reinforcements closed in.

The Magistracy of Canopus adopted the design with enthusiasm. Magistracy Armed Forces commanders prize Shen Long assignments as a mark of distinction, though the honor carries high casualty rates and routine exposure to difficult engagements.

The Shen Long's quad chassis carries 1,500 kilograms at a ground speed of 43 kilometers per hour, outpacing most heavy battlesuits in Inner Sphere arsenals. Its mimetic armor system uses 550 kilograms of specialized coating to distort visual and electronic sensor returns, granting significant concealment advantages. The modular turret mount provides 400 kilograms of interchangeable payload capacity while the four-legged design eliminates manipulator capability.

The machine gun configuration loads four machine guns into the turret, each carrying fifty rounds of ammunition. This loadout delivers withering anti-infantry firepower and can threaten exposed rear armor on vehicles and BattleMechs through sustained volume of fire. The deep ammunition reserves provide longer endurance than many other Shen Long configurations. Machine guns struggle against armored targets at range, however, limiting this configuration to close engagements and soft-target suppression.

Weighing 1,500 kilograms, the Shen Long employs a quad chassis that provides a ground speed of 43 kilometers per hour, placing the suit among the fastest heavy battlesuits available to Inner Sphere forces. Its 550 kilograms of mimetic armor grants both protection and active camouflage, allowing troopers to approach targets undetected before opening fire. The suit's modular turret mount accommodates 400 kilograms of interchangeable weapons.

The MRM configuration fits a five-tube medium range missile launcher in the turret with enough ammunition for four volleys. This loadout provides the greatest effective engagement range among the missile-armed configurations, enabling troopers to strike from beyond the reach of most infantry weapons. The missiles can deliver punishing damage against clustered targets or lightly armored vehicles. The limited ammunition supply restricts the configuration to short, sharp engagements, and the launcher's bulk leaves no room for secondary weapons or equipment.

At 1,500 kilograms on a quad chassis, the Shen Long reaches 43 kilometers per hour, faster than almost any other heavy battlesuit in the Inner Sphere. Mimetic armor weighing 550 kilograms provides both physical protection and active camouflage, bending light and sensor returns to mask the suit's position. The modular turret mount accepts 400 kilograms of interchangeable weapons, though the four-legged chassis eliminates all manipulator capability.

The SRM configuration mounts a four-tube short range missile launcher in the turret, carrying enough ammunition for four volleys. The SRM-4 delivers the heaviest single-salvo damage of any Shen Long configuration, making it the preferred loadout for anti-BattleMech ambushes where troopers can close to effective range under concealment. The missiles hit hard enough to threaten even assault-class targets at close quarters. Ammunition limitations and the short effective range constrain the configuration to carefully planned engagements where troopers can strike and withdraw before being targeted.

The Simian is a medium-class Inner Sphere battle armor designed for mass production and easy maintenance. Conceived under a Republic of the Sphere program to reduce the rising cost of powered infantry, the suit prioritizes affordability and field serviceability over technological sophistication. Rhodes Foundry of Devil's Rock brought the design into production in 3135, creating a general-purpose combat suit built entirely from standard Inner Sphere components. Jump-capable and equipped with magnetic claws for anti-vehicle operations, the Simian fills a skirmisher role, relying on speed and agility rather than heavy armor to protect its operators. A modular weapon mount allows field-level customization of the primary armament.

This configuration replaces the standard weapon with a Flamer on the modular mount, trading ranged precision for area-denial and anti-infantry capability. The flamer proves devastating in confined spaces and against unarmored targets, making this loadout well suited to urban clearance and building-to-building fighting. Magnetic claws on both arms provide melee capability and allow troopers to conduct swarming attacks against larger targets. A searchlight is also fitted.

Weighing one thousand kilograms with 350 kilograms of standard armor, the suit maintains the medium weight classification shared across all Simian configurations. The armor provides adequate protection against small arms fire but cannot absorb hits from dedicated anti-armor weapons. Above-average ground speed and a 90-meter jump range give troopers the mobility to close rapidly with targets, which complements the flamer's short effective range. This variant sees frequent use in close-assault roles where the combination of fire, speed, and magnetic claws overwhelms defenders.

The Simian emerged from a Republic of the Sphere initiative to reduce the prohibitive cost of battle armor production. Paladin Kara Rutherford championed the program, commissioning a design study that prioritized affordability and ease of maintenance over advanced technology. Rutherford did not live to see the project reach fruition. Rhodes Foundry on Devil's Rock brought the suit into production in 3135, working behind the secrecy of the Republic's collapsing borders.

The suit entered service as a tool of Exarch Jonah Levin's campaign to destabilize the Republic's rivals through deniable operations. Substantial numbers were manufactured in the months before April 3136, and troopers wearing the Simian fought across every realm bordering the Republic in false-flag formations. During campaigns in the Draconis March, RAF units masquerading as Davion forces employed Simians extensively alongside conventional forces. On Galatea in 3144, disguised Republic operatives used small craft to insert platoons of Simians directly onto Jade Falcon positions. The suit's deliberate simplicity, using common Inner Sphere components and standard weaponry, meant that virtually any industrial base could replicate it. This proliferation ensured the Simian spread well beyond Republic control as the Dark Age conflicts intensified.

Fitted with a Light Recoilless Rifle on its modular weapon mount, this configuration gives the Simian a ballistic option with better range than the standard energy loadout. The rifle provides reasonable hitting power against soft targets, though its ammunition dependency limits sustained operations. Magnetic claws on both arms remain available for close-quarters combat and anti-vehicle swarming attacks, with a searchlight completing the equipment fit.

The suit's 350 kilograms of standard armor offer moderate protection at one thousand kilograms total weight, keeping the design within the medium class. Ground speed and 90-meter jump capability exceed most comparable battle armor designs, allowing troopers to use terrain and mobility to offset the armor's limitations. The recoilless rifle configuration favors engagements at medium range, where operators can pick targets from cover before closing or withdrawing as the tactical situation demands.

The Simian mounts a Small Laser on a modular weapon mount positioned on the right shoulder, providing a reliable energy weapon that requires no ammunition. Magnetic claws on both arms serve as effective melee weapons against infantry and allow troopers to latch onto enemy vehicles and BattleMechs for swarming attacks. A searchlight rounds out the equipment package.

At one thousand kilograms, the suit falls within the medium weight class and carries 350 kilograms of standard armor. This protection is adequate against small arms and light weapons but insufficient to withstand sustained fire from heavier systems. The Simian compensates with above-average ground speed and a 90-meter jump capability that allows troopers to reposition quickly between engagements. The laser configuration works best at close range, where operators can exploit the suit's agility to close distance and engage with both the laser and magnetic claws in rapid succession.

shared: The Sloth was one of the first battle armor designs developed natively by the Inner Sphere. A team at the New Avalon Institute of Science, drawing on captured Clan technology, produced a heavy quadruped suit intended to serve as a mobile weapons platform capable of engaging enemy battle armor directly. Unlike the humanoid designs that would follow, the Sloth adopted a four-legged configuration more commonly associated with combat vehicles than powered infantry. Introduced in 3050 alongside its lighter companion, the Infiltrator, the Sloth earned a mixed reputation among field commanders. Its firepower and protection drew praise, but the unconventional design and its inherent limitations left many formations seeking alternatives as newer suits entered production.

The Huntsman refit strips the Sloth to its chassis and rebuilds it as a dedicated battle armor hunter. Two King David light gauss rifles replace all previous armament, providing accurate kinetic fire against armored infantry targets at range. Improved stealth armor replaces the original standard plating, reducing the suit's sensor signature while maintaining protective capability. A mechanical jump booster grants limited vertical mobility, a capability the base Sloth never possessed.

These upgrades transform the platform from a static weapons emplacement into a mobile ambush predator well-suited to stalking hostile battle armor in broken terrain and urban environments. The quad chassis retains its signature low profile, complementing the stealth systems. The Huntsman still lacks manipulators, but its role as a ranged hunter rather than a close-combat brawler makes this less of a liability.

The Sloth was developed at the New Avalon Institute of Science by a predominantly Lyran design team. The program began after the 1st Somerset Strikers captured Clan Elemental data during a raid in the early stages of Operation REVIVAL. The Federated Commonwealth launched parallel development efforts, producing the lightweight Infiltrator scout suit alongside the heavier Sloth.

NAIS designers diverged from the Elemental's humanoid configuration, opting for a quadruped chassis that shared more in common with miniaturized combat vehicles than conventional battle armor. This approach simplified myomer integration and eliminated bipedal balance challenges, accelerating both development and pilot training.

The prototype underwent live-fire testing on Waldorff V, where a surprise Clan Jade Falcon attack produced the first recorded instance of an Inner Sphere battle armor trooper destroying an enemy BattleMech in combat. The Commonwealth approved the Sloth for full production in 3050.

Limited numbers deployed throughout the Federated Commonwealth, but the Federated Suns' high command never embraced the design. Production shifted to Lyran factories, and after the Lyran Alliance seceded in 3057, TharHes Industries continued building Sloths in limited quantities until the Fenrir replaced it around 3060. Surviving suits persisted in service with various formations, including mercenary commands. Later refits during the Jihad and Dark Age eras extended the chassis into specialized roles.

The Interdictor variant trades the standard model's pop-up mine and small lasers for an ECM suite and a pair of extended-range small lasers. The electronic countermeasures package disrupts enemy targeting and communications networks, giving the Interdictor a battlefield support role that the original design never possessed. The upgraded lasers provide improved reach while maintaining comparable damage output.

The Interdictor retains the base chassis characteristics: quadruped movement, 250 kilograms of standard armor, and no manipulators. The same trade-offs that defined the original Sloth apply here, with the suit unable to perform swarming attacks or ride OmniMech handholds. The ECM capability proved particularly effective against Word of Blake forces during the Jihad, where disrupting command and control systems added tactical value that extended the aging design's operational relevance.
